title: Neurocognitive and Sensory Development Following Frontoorbital Advancement for Craniosynostosis—A Follow-Up Study in Childhood
summary: The aim of this study is to examine olfactory function (sense of smell) and neurocognitive (mental) development in children several years after frontoorbital advancement surgery (surgical correction of the skull shape). For this study, we would like to test children between the ages of 5 and 10 once, over a limited period of time, using two smell tests, an IQ screening test, and a clinical examination. Overall, there is not yet much data available on these specific assessments following surgery. We therefore intend to conduct this study to help plan better follow-up care.
conditions: Possible complication following fronto-orbital advancement for craniosynostosis.

interventions.name:
Children and parents are offered the opportunity to participate in the study during a follow-up consultation regarding craniosynostosis and surgical treatment using frontoorbital advancement. If they consent and participate, the following parameters will be collected or examined:
Olfactory function

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The study will include children between the ages of 5 and 10 who underwent surgical correction of craniosynostosis during their first or second year of life via open fronto-orbital remodeling or advancement at the Department of Pediatric Surgery at Dresden University Hospital. Minimally invasive treatments performed in newborns or early infancy are not included. Furthermore, consent to participate in the study must be obtained from the legal guardians and, if applicable, from the child.
Exclusion criteria:
Known genetic syndromes associated with cognitive impairments
Known neurological disorders
Preterm birth < 32 weeks of gestation
Incomplete documentation of the surgery or follow-up care
